reason: Clarify scalar distance comparison with displacement magnitude, exactly as upstream.
before: <para id="import-auto-id1752774">We have noted that distance traveled can be greater than displacement. So average speed can be greater than average velocity, which is displacement divided by time. For example, if you drive to a store and return home in half an hour, and your car’s odometer shows the total distance traveled was 6 km, then your average speed was 12 km/h. Your average velocity, however, was zero, because your displacement for the round trip is zero. (Displacement is change in position and, thus, is zero for a round trip.) Thus average speed is <emphasis effect="italics">not</emphasis> simply the magnitude of average velocity.</para>
